The returned `node` still owns the element that was not inserted, so `empty()` is false. That is the point of `insert_return_type`: a failed insertion does not destroy the element you extracted.

Extraction invalidates only iterators to the element; pointers and references to it stay valid, and they may not be used while a node handle owns the element. Once the element is inserted again, they are usable and refer to the same object, so `r += "!"` modifies it. options: Undefined behavior: an empty node handle has no key to compare
questions.explanation: Inserting an empty node handle is specified: it has no effect and returns `inserted == false`, `position == end()` and an empty `node`. It is the accessors `key()`, `value()` and `get_allocator()` on an empty handle that are undefined. `111` is tempting for those who expect a successful no-op to report success.

questions.prompt: What is the status of the transfer of a node between these two maps?

Well-formed: the node is reallocated from `a`'s resource
Well-formed: allocators are never consulted when inserting a node
questions.explanation: `insert(node_type&&)` requires the node handle's allocator to compare equal to the container's. A `polymorphic_allocator` compares equal only when both use the same memory resource, and these use different ones, so the precondition is violated. Nothing is reallocated: node transfer relinks the existing node, which is why the allocators must agree.
